objective:
Add word-prefix search to the item catalogue, with a `--search` option for the `items` command.

In `stockroom/textutil.py` add `words(text: str) -> list[str]`: the lower-cased runs of ASCII letters `a-z` and digits `0-9` of `text`, in order; every other character (spaces, punctuation, hyphens and non-ASCII letters included) separates words. `words("Blue Mug, 2x")` is `["blue", "mug", "2x"]`, `words("NB-200")` is `["nb", "200"]` and `words("naïve")` is `["na", "ve"]`.

Create the module `stockroom/catalogue.py` with `search(items: Iterable[Item], query: str) -> list[Item]`.

The words of an item are the `words()` of its name, of its SKU and of each of its tags (the name words are also called its name words). A query word matches an item when it is a prefix of at least one word of the item (a word is a prefix of itself). An item is in the result only when every word of the query (`words(query)`) matches it.

The result is ordered best first by this key, compared in turn: (1) the number of query words that are equal to a word of the item, larger first; (2) the number of query words that are a prefix of a name word of the item, larger first; (3) the SKU, ascending in Python's default `str` order. Both numbers count query words, so a word that occurs twice in the query counts twice. Items with a full tie keep their input order. A query without any word (empty, only spaces or punctuation) matches every item: the result is all items in their input order. The result is a new list; `items` may be any iterable and is not modified.

Add the option `--search QUERY` to the `items` command (`python -m stockroom items --file ITEMS.csv [--tag TAG] [--search QUERY]`). The `--tag` filter works as before and is applied first; `search` is then applied to the remaining items, and the table lists the result in the search order. Without `--search` the command behaves exactly as before. A search without any match prints the table header and rule lines only, exit code 0.
acceptance: textutil.words returns the lower-cased runs of ASCII letters and digits, treating every other character (including non-ASCII letters) as a separator
search matches an item only if every query word is a prefix of some word of the item's name, SKU or tags (SKU and tags are split into words too)
search orders results by: most query words equal to an item word, then most query words that prefix a name word (counted per query word, repeats count), then SKU ascending; full ties keep input order
A query without words returns all items in input order; search returns a new list, accepts any iterable and does not modify its input; no match gives []
The items command takes --search, applies --tag first, then search, and prints the table in search order; with no match only the header and rule lines are printed; without --search nothing changes
